title: Quantization assurance: baseline signatures, CI gating, and rollout/rollback automation
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Create an operationally robust mechanism to capture per-model quantization 'assurance signatures' (calibration artifacts + baseline metrics), wire those artifacts into CI gating for FP8/INT8 profile promotion in the model catalog, and implement automated canary rollouts with fast rollback hooks. This ticket focuses on the engineering integration: artifact format, storage, CI thresholds, and rollout automation scripts. UX/catalog metadata work will be a follow-up (PM ticket).
acceptance_criteria: Define a compact assurance signature format (artifact manifest) that contains calibration vectors, representative token distributions, golden outputs on validation prompts, and quant config metadata for FP8 and INT8 profiles
Implement artifact serializer and validator (python tool) that produces a deterministic SHA256 signature for each model+profile
Store artifacts in S3 path with predictable naming and lifecycle policy (see artifacts_location) and surface URL in model catalog metadata
Integrate a CI gating step: pull assurance artifact, run fast-delta validation on a small canonical eval set, and fail promotion when regression exceeds threshold (see ci_checks)
Implement a canary rollout job that deploys quant profile to 5% of traffic, measures key metrics for 60 minutes, and automatically rolls back if any critical check is violated
Provide operation runbook describing how to recover from false positives and how to force-promote when necessary
tasks: Spec: draft assurance signature manifest spec and sample artifacts
Implementation: serializer/validator binaries (python) and unit tests
Storage: S3 path, IAM policy, lifecycle rules
CI: add pipeline stage in catalog-promotion job and implement fast-delta evaluator harness
Rollout: canary orchestration script (k8s job + Catalog API hooks) and rollback automation
Docs: runbook + operator guide + one-pager for PM/Design
experiment_results_summary: Experiment: quant-profile FP8-a on xglm-3b using INT8-like calibration vectors
Dataset: 200 canonical prompts sampled from prod-like prompt buckets (chat, completion, instruction)
Metric: delta-BLEU-like relevance proxy and token-level perplexity; measured end-to-end latency
Result: FP8-a showed mean delta-relevance -0.6% (within threshold), tail token error spikes on 0.7% of prompts primarily on long-context math items
Action: include targeted calibration vectors for long-context math as part of artifact for models with >1024 context
ci_checks: Golden-output delta: no more than 1.2% mean degradation on canonical set
Worst-case prompt regression: no single prompt may exceed 8% degradation
Latency SLO: p95 latency increase < 12% compared to float baseline for same batch size
Memory: peak GPU memory within profile budget (+-5%)
Sanity fuzz: end-to-end decode must not produce invalid UTF sequences or structurally malformed JSON when structured-output schema is provided
rollout_plan: Stage 0: Artifact produced and validated locally by serializer/validator
Stage 1: CI promotion job runs fast-delta evaluation; if passes, model catalog entry marked 'quant-ready' with artifact URL
Stage 2: Canary deploy (5% traffic) for 60 minutes with telemetry hooks (latency, relevance proxy, per-prompt regression alerts)
Stage 3: If canary passes, incrementally increase to 25% for 3 hours, then 100% with observation window
Stage 4: Post-promotion audit job runs full calibration suite and archives results
rollback_plan: Automatic rollback triggered when any critical CI check fails during canary or when runtime alert fires (configurable): revert to previous quant profile and mark catalog entry 'needs-investigation'
Manual rollback: operator may run 'catalog rollback --model <id> --profile <previous>' which triggers immediate traffic re-route and a hotfix job
Forcing promotion: ops can add 'force=true' in promotion job only after cross-team approval; this action creates an incident ticket automatically
notes: We intentionally keep assurance signature compact (~5-20MB) to keep CI runtime under 10 minutes for the fast-delta pass
Calibration vectors must include token frequency histogram + 3 representative long-context cases when model context > 1024
This ticket avoids changing catalog UI; PM will own metadata display follow-up (PM-401)
We considered using OCI registry for artifacts but chose S3 for faster retrieval from CI runners and predictable ACLs
Edge case: models that use custom tokenizer require token-mapped golden outputs inside artifact
decisions: Use SHA256 over the serialized manifest for deterministic signature
Fast-delta CI check uses a 200-prompt canonical set with weighted buckets to reflect production distribution
Canary default: 5% traffic for 60 minutes; threshold and window configurable per-model via catalog metadata
risks: False negatives: fast-delta set may miss rare failure modes leading to late-stage regressions
Operational complexity: more artifacts to manage increases S3 costs and retention policy decisions
Rollback flapping: aggressive automated rollback may oscillate on noisy metrics; need cooldown windows
